turn.user_message: How would we know it is working?
turn.context: Prompt 3 of bm-au-07 and bm-pr-07. Transcript 29 (eight numbers, checked weekly, six new; occupancy and stay tracked, not promised) and bed-management.md §8 (with dead bed time and stage times added, as agreed). The day background returns here.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · Processes, turn 9 (the record stops at 31)

text: Eight numbers, read every week. Six of them nobody measures today.
bullets: Start with dead bed time. It moves when any of the others improve, and both halves sit in your billing system.
Three numbers check people are doing the new thing. If they slip, the rest follows within a fortnight.
Occupancy and length of stay are tracked, not promised. This work moves time and billing.
chat.invite: Next, we can plan a trial on one ward.
prompts: Can we try it on one ward first?
Who would read these each week?
chat.pointer: Pick a window to see how it is measured. Switch to see which are read in the trial.

blocks.title: Eight windows, read weekly
blocks.deck: Each measure as a window on the station wall. Six are new and start with no number.

measures.name: Dead bed time, bill to bill
Discharge dates given a day ahead

blocks.condition: Read every week, not every month. A month hides a bad week.

sheets.title: Dead bed time, bill to bill
sheets.text: From the last bill of one patient to the first bill of the next, on the same bed. The one number that moves when the others improve.
sheets.entry: Has billing ever looked at this?

sheets.title: Admission time, step by step
sheets.text: Your 3½ hours, split into its five steps. It shows paperwork apart from waiting.
sheets.entry: Which step do you think is slowest?

sheets.title: Beds planned by 6 PM
sheets.text: How many of tomorrow’s planned patients have a bed by 6 PM. An early warning if it slips.
sheets.entry: How many planned admissions in a usual day?

sheets.title: Discharge dates given a day ahead
sheets.text: How many discharges had a confirmed date 24 hours before. Shows if the round is working.
sheets.entry: How many discharges have a date today?

sheets.title: Admissions finished by noon
sheets.text: The share of planned patients in bed by about noon. Shows if the new order is holding.
sheets.entry: How many patients are in bed by noon today?

sheets.title: Likely stay against real stay
sheets.text: How close the likely dates were to the real ones, by procedure. Keeps the predictions honest.

sheets.title: Bed occupancy
sheets.text: Tracked as it is today. Not expected to rise much. That is not what this work does.

sheets.title: Average length of stay
sheets.text: Tracked as it is today. It may fall a little. That gain is already counted once in the money.
sheets.entry: Is length of stay tracked by ward?

blocks.label: Expected to change
blocks.sub: Occupancy will not go up. Patients reach a bed earlier, and each bed earns for more of the day.
